title: Clerk Pricing 2026: Free, Pro and Business Plans
summary: Clerk pricing starts with a free tier and scales as your user count grows. Choose your plan based on the features and user limits you require.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


These are the questions the monthly review tends to raise. The answers come from Clerk's pricing page and docs as written in November 2026. Plans change, so confirm each answer on the page it points to before you act.


### Is Clerk free for production apps?


Yes, Clerk's free plan can run a live app, not just a test project, up to the monthly active user allowance listed on its pricing page. The catch's that some features sit only on paid plans.


If your launch plan needs one of them, the free tier isn't really free for you. Read the feature comparison on the pricing page against your own list before you launch.


### Does Clerk charge per user or per monthly active user?


Not everyone who has ever signed up gets billed. Clerk bills on monthly active users. A dormant account that never comes back shouldn't run up your bill.


The exact rule for when someone counts as active is in Clerk's docs on billing and usage, and you should read it, because that definition's the number your invoice is built on.


Can you cancel or downgrade Clerk mid-month? You can change your plan from the billing section of the Clerk dashboard, and no phone call is required.


What I can't tell you is how your current billing period is treated when you do. Check Clerk's billing documentation first, then make the change early in a cycle so a mistake costs you less.


Does Clerk offer discounts for startups or nonprofits? Don't assume so, and don't budget around one. The pricing page's the only place to confirm whether a startup or nonprofit offer exists today.


If none is listed, a short message to Clerk's sales or support team costs you nothing and gives you an answer in writing. Plan your numbers at list price until you have that answer.


### What happens if I exceed the free tier limit?


You'll need a paid plan, and waiting to find out is the expensive way to learn the details. Clerk's pricing page explains how usage above an included allowance is handled.


Put an alert on your user count well below the limit, so the upgrade's a decision you make on your schedule and not a surprise on an invoice.
